t: Persepolis was raised on a great terrace by Darius I from about 519 to 515 BCE, and Xerxes I and later kings added to it until the downfall of the Achaemenid Empire.
It was a ceremonial complex used seasonally rather than one of the largest cities of the empire, and its function, including where the king's private quarters stood, is still not entirely clear.
Alexander the Great took it in 330 BCE, and soon afterwards its wooden parts were destroyed by fire; its ruins were visited by European travellers from the 15th century and excavated from 1930.
dyk: The study of the trilingual royal inscriptions found on the ruins of Persepolis led to the initial decipherment of cuneiform in the early 19th century.
ev: Construction of the broad stairway of the terrace begins
Date of the earliest remains and of the coin hoard laid under the foundation boxes of the Apadana
Darius I dies, and Xerxes I completes the Tachara palace
Alexander the Great takes Persepolis, and a fire destroys its palaces
Persepolis is still the capital of Persia as a province of the Macedonian Empire
The Sasanian prince Shapur Sakanshah leaves an inscription naming the site Sad-stun
García de Silva Figueroa links Chehel Minar with the Persepolis of the classical authors
Ernst Herzfeld and Erich Schmidt begin the first scientific excavations

f.founded: The earliest remains date to 515 BCE; Darius I built the terrace and the palaces, and the French archaeologist André Godard believed that Cyrus the Great had chosen the site.
f.where: On a terrace leaning on Rahmat Mountain, near the small river Pulvar, in the plains of Marvdasht, encircled by the southern Zagros Mountains, in Fars province of Iran.
f.known: The Apadana and its stairway reliefs; the Gate of All Nations; the Hundred-Columns Palace; the Tachara and Hadish palaces; the burning of the palaces in 330 BCE; the Persepolis Fortification Archive; the trilingual royal inscriptions that helped the decipherment of cuneiform
f.today: Persepolis is a ruin and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Fars province, Iran.
